subject: Problem with the creation of a camera station table

messages.author: 6822344c9c5a3d37
messages.subject: Problem with the creation of a camera station table
parts:
Hi there,

Like several others, I imported my data from an existing Excel file. While my species table is working perfectly fine with camtrapR, I'm encountering a problem with the camera station table. I can't perform any functions with it because it doesn't register as a dataframe and I keep getting the following warning message:

Error: CTtable must be a data.frame
In addition: Warning message:
In if (class(CTtable) != "data.frame") stop("CTtable must be a data.frame",  :
  the condition has length > 1 and only the first element will be used

Attached is the table I've constructed in Excel that mimics the camtraps table and has the necessary columns for species, station, co-ordinates, setup and retrieval dates.

Is there something I can do in order to get this to work?

Thanks so much for your help!
Ayesha

Your’s is an orthodox station file. So the problem is elsewhere.
How are you bringing it into R and camtrapR?

David

messages.subject: Re: Problem with the creation of a camera station table
parts:
A

I will be corrected but my understanding is tidyverse uses tibles and data frames. camtrapR uses base R , data frames only.  
Your script would have worked if you assign your statement as.dataframe(CameraStationTable) to the same or a new object, i.e. (I think; I will try in a minute)
CameraStationTable <- as.data.frame(CameraStationTable)

D

#                                                 utm_x = col_integer(), utm_y = col_integer()))

parts: Good.  I’m glad.   There is a tension in the community - some of us want to stay with base R while others want to use the tidyverse tools and modern R.  Jeurgen's scripts are very meticulous in checking the formats and the classes and I believe he only uses data frames not the tidyverse tibles.  We need to persdaude Jeurgen to explain that tidyverse will not work with camtrapR.
